topics: 🕯️ Shmuel HaKatan Forgets His Own Blessing — why he was not removed, and whether a good person can turn wicked
🔢 Seven, Nine, Twenty-Four — the Shabbat, Rosh HaShana, and fast-day Amida and what they correspond to
✂️ Havineinu — Rav vs. Shmuel on the abridged Amida, Abaye's curse, and when it may not be said
🌧️ Errors and Omissions — rain, havdala, and Rosh Ḥodesh: when one must return to the beginning

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Short Prayers and Missed Words
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 29a–29b
overview.hebrewSource: הֲבִינֵנוּ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ לָדַעַת דְּרָכֶיךָ… טֶרֶם נִקְרָא אַתָּה תַעֲנֶה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: Shmuel HaKatan, who composed the blessing against heretics, forgot it the next year and was left standing for hours without being removed — the Gemara asks why, and along the way debates whether a righteous person can become wicked, using Yoḥanan the High Priest as the test case. After counting the blessings of the Shabbat, Rosh HaShana, and fast-day Amida, the daf turns to Rabbi Yehoshua's abridged Amida: Shmuel's 'Havineinu' text, and why it cannot be used on motzaei Shabbat or in the rainy season. That leads to Rabbi Tanḥum's rules for one who forgot rain, havdala, or Rosh Ḥodesh. The daf closes with four definitions of a 'fixed' prayer, the meaning of 'parashat ha'ibur', the brief prayers for a place of danger, and the traveler's prayer.

slides.title: 🕯️ Why Wasn't Shmuel HaKatan Removed?
slides.subtitle: He forgot the blessing of the heretics, scrutinized it for two or three hours, and stayed as prayer leader

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: Rav Yehuda said in Rav's name: one who errs in any blessing is not removed, but in the blessing of the heretics he is removed — we suspect he is a heretic. So why not Shmuel HaKatan?

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: Shmuel HaKatan is different: he instituted the blessing himself.

lines.speaker: Abaye
lines.text: We have a tradition: a good person does not become wicked (טָבָא לָא הָוֵי בִּישָׁא). Ezekiel 18:24, 'when the righteous returns from his righteousness', speaks of one wicked from the outset who repented and relapsed.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: But the mishna says 'do not trust yourself until the day you die' — Yoḥanan the High Priest served eighty years and became a Sadducee!

lines.speaker: Abaye / Rava
lines.text: Abaye: Yannai and Yoḥanan are the same man, wicked from the outset. Rava: they are two — Yannai wicked from the start, Yoḥanan righteous from the start. So for Rava, even the initially righteous may change.

lines.speaker: Final answer
lines.text: Shmuel HaKatan is different because he had begun the blessing. Rav (or Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi): removal applies only where he never began it; if he began, he may finish.

callout.label: Corresponding to what?
callout.text: Seven Shabbat blessings — the seven 'voices' of David over the waters (Psalm 29), per Rabbi Ḥalafta ben Shaul. Nine of Rosh HaShana — Hannah's nine mentions of God's name, for on Rosh HaShana Sarah, Rachel, and Hannah were remembered (Rabbi Yitzḥak of Kartignin). Twenty-four of fast days — Solomon's twenty-four songs when the ark entered the Holy of Holies, said on a day of mercy (Rabbi Ḥelbo).

slides.title: ✂️ Havineinu: The Abridged Amida and Its Limits
slides.subtitle: What is Rabbi Yehoshua's 'abridgement of the eighteen'?

nodes.content: ❓ Rav: an abridged form of each blessing. Shmuel: one blessing, 'Havineinu' (הֲבִינֵנוּ), replacing the thirteen middle blessings and ending 'Who listens to prayer'
⚠️ Abaye would curse anyone who prayed Havineinu — it is only for exigent circumstances

columns.label: Not on motzaei Shabbat / Festivals
columns.content: Rav Naḥman in Shmuel's name: havdala must be said in 'Who graciously grants knowledge'

columns.label: Not in the rainy season
columns.content: Rav Beivai bar Abaye: the request for rain must be said in 'the blessing of the years'

nodes.content: 🗣️ Rabba bar Shmuel: say havdala as a fourth blessing, like Rabbi Akiva? — No: they instituted seven, not eight, just as we do not follow Rabbi Akiva all year (eighteen, not nineteen)

🗣️ Mar Zutra: fold it in — 'Havineinu… Who distinguishes sacred from profane'? For havdala: kashya, unanswered. For rain, 'satisfy us… and grant dew and rain'? He will become confused — a change in the middle confuses, at the beginning it does not
🗣️ Rav Ashi: put rain in 'Who listens to prayer', as one who forgot may? — One who erred is different; not ab initio

callout.label: Havineinu's requests:
callout.text: Understanding, repentance, forgiveness, redemption, healing, prosperity, ingathering, judgment, the wicked, the righteous, Jerusalem, David's line — 'before we call, You answer'.

slides.title: 🌧️ Forgot Rain, Havdala, or Rosh Ḥodesh — Go Back?
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Tanḥum in the name of Rav Asi, and the Tosefta that seems to contradict him

boxes.title: Must return to the beginning
items: Omitted 'the might of the rains' in 'Who revives the dead' — always
Omitted the request for rain in 'the blessing of the years' and remembered only after 'Who listens to prayer' (the Tosefta's case)
Omitted Rosh Ḥodesh in the Temple-service blessing and already finished and moved his feet (Rav Pappa son of Rav Aḥa bar Adda, from Rav)

boxes.title: Need not return to the beginning
items: Omitted the request for rain but remembered before 'Who listens to prayer' — he asks there
Omitted havdala in 'Who graciously grants knowledge' — he can say it over the cup of wine
Omitted Rosh Ḥodesh and remembered in thanksgiving or 'Grant peace' — he returns only to the Temple-service blessing
Finished but still standing, or accustomed to supplications after the Amida — he returns to Temple service (Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak; a second version reverses the last condition)

callout.label: Rejected harmonization:
callout.text: The Gemara first suggested the strict Tosefta speaks of an individual and the lenient ruling of a congregation that hears the prayer leader. But then Rabbi Tanḥum should have said 'because he hears it from the leader', not 'because he can say it in Who listens to prayer'. So both speak of an individual, and the difference is before or after that blessing.

slides.title: 📿 'One Whose Prayer Is Fixed' — Four Definitions
slides.subtitle: The mishna: Rabbi Eliezer says one who makes his prayer keva (קֶבַע), his prayer is not supplication
rows: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi in the name of Rabbi Oshaya
Anyone for whom prayer is like a burden (כְּמַשּׂוֹי)
He wants only to be rid of it
Anyone who does not say it in the language of supplication
Anyone unable to add something new (לְחַדֵּשׁ בָּהּ דָּבָר)
Rabbi Zeira: I could add something new, but I fear I would become confused
Abaye bar Avin and Rabbi Ḥanina bar Avin
Anyone who does not pray with the reddening of the sun (דִּמְדּוּמֵי חַמָּה)
Rabbi Yoḥanan: it is a mitzva; Rabbi Zeira: 'let them fear You with the sun and before the moon' (Psalms 72:5)

callout.label: But in the West:
callout.text: In Eretz Yisrael they cursed one who prays with the reddening of the sun before sunset — he may be distracted, lose track of the hour, and miss the time for prayer altogether.

slides.title: 🛣️ Brief Prayers for Danger and the Traveler's Prayer
slides.subtitle: The mishna: one walking in a place of danger says a short prayer 'at every parashat ha'ibur'

steps.content: 1️⃣ What is פָּרָשַׁת הָעִבּוּר? Rav Ḥisda in Mar Ukva's name: even when You are filled with anger (עֶבְרָה) at them like a pregnant woman (עוּבָּרָה) — or, even when they transgress (עוֹבְרִים) the Torah — may their needs be before You

2️⃣ The Tosefta's brief prayers for a place of wild beasts and robbers: Rabbi Eliezer — 'Do Your will in heaven above and give calm to those who fear You below'; Rabbi Yehoshua — 'Hear the cry of Your people Israel'; Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok — 'Hear the shout of Your people'
3️⃣ Aḥerim: 'The needs of Your people Israel are many and their understanding is short… give each one his sustenance and each body what it lacks.' Rav Huna: the halakha follows Aḥerim
4️⃣ Elijah to Rav Yehuda, brother of Rav Sala Ḥasida: do not get angry and you will not sin; do not get drunk and you will not sin; and when you set out on the road, consult your Creator and go
5️⃣ Rabbi Ya'akov in Rav Ḥisda's name: 'consult your Creator' is the traveler's prayer (תְּפִלַּת הַדֶּרֶךְ), and whoever sets out must recite it

6️⃣ The text: lead me in peace, direct my steps in peace, support me in peace, save me from every enemy and ambush, bless the work of my hands, grant me grace, kindness, and mercy in Your eyes and in the eyes of all who see me — Blessed… Who hears prayer

callout.label: All end alike:
callout.text: Every brief formula, and the traveler's prayer, closes with the blessing 'Who listens to prayer' (שׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלָּה).

summary.principle: A prayer leader who began the blessing of the heretics may finish it; an abridged Amida is only for emergencies and never where havdala or rain must be inserted; and prayer must be supplication, not a fixed burden.

flowSteps.content: 🕯️ Shmuel HaKatan forgets the blessing he wrote → not removed, because he had begun it
❓ Can a good person turn wicked? Abaye: no (Yannai = Yoḥanan); Rava: yes (Yoḥanan the High Priest)
✂️ Havineinu (Shmuel's text) — not on motzaei Shabbat (havdala) nor in the rainy season (request for rain)

columns.content: 🌧️ Forgot rain: repeat if past 'Who listens to prayer'; forgot havdala: say it on the cup; forgot Rosh Ḥodesh: back to Temple service, or to the start if he moved his feet
📿 'Fixed' prayer = a burden, no supplication, nothing new, or not with the sun's reddening

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: in danger, the short prayer of Aḥerim; on the road, 'consult your Creator' — the traveler's prayer is an obligation

quiz.q: What is the Gemara's final explanation for why Shmuel HaKatan was not removed as prayer leader when he forgot the blessing of the heretics?
o: Because a good person never becomes wicked
Because he had already begun the blessing, and one who began may finish it
Because the congregation had no replacement
Because the blessing was not yet obligatory
quiz.e: After Rava's view leaves open that even the initially righteous can change, the Gemara answers that Shmuel HaKatan had begun reciting the blessing. Rav (or Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi) taught that removal applies only to one who did not begin it.

quiz.q: According to Rabba and Rav Yosef, what makes a prayer 'fixed' (keva)?
o: Praying at the same hour every day
Praying without facing the Temple
Being unable to introduce something new into it
Praying after the reddening of the sun
quiz.e: Rabba and Rav Yosef define keva as the inability to add a novel, personal element. Rabbi Zeira remarked that he could do so but feared becoming confused, so this is not demanded of everyone.

quiz.q: Why may Havineinu not be recited in the evening prayer at the conclusion of Shabbat?
o: Because it is too short to be said at night
Because havdala must be recited in the blessing 'Who graciously grants knowledge'
Because Abaye cursed anyone who says it
Because the request for rain must be included
quiz.e: Rav Naḥman in Shmuel's name excludes motzaei Shabbat and Festivals because havdala belongs in 'Who graciously grants knowledge', which Havineinu replaces. Mar Zutra's proposal to fold havdala into Havineinu was left unanswered (kashya).

quiz.q: An individual forgot the request for rain in 'the blessing of the years' and remembered before reaching 'Who listens to prayer'. What does he do?
o: He returns to the beginning of the Amida
He returns to 'the blessing of the years'
He inserts the request in 'Who listens to prayer' and continues
He omits it and makes up for it in the next prayer
quiz.e: The Gemara resolves the contradiction between Rabbi Tanḥum and the Tosefta by timing: if he remembers before 'Who listens to prayer', he asks there; if only after it, he must return to the beginning.

quiz.q: Whose version of the brief prayer for a place of danger does Rav Huna rule is the halakha?
o: Rabbi Eliezer's: 'Do Your will in the heavens above'
Rabbi Yehoshua's: 'Hear the cry of Your people Israel'
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok's: 'Hear the shout of Your people'
Aḥerim's: 'The needs of Your people Israel are many and their understanding is short'
quiz.e: Rav Huna rules in accordance with Aḥerim, whose formula asks God to give each person his sustenance and each body what it lacks, ending 'Blessed are You, Lord, Who listens to prayer'.
